The variable aperture lens of the shiny new iPhone 18 Pro goes almost one stop wider than the fixed aperture lens in its predecessor: up from f/1.78 in the iPhone 17 Pro to f/1.48 (a smaller number is wider).

In principle, this will allow for slightly shallower depth of field, enabling greater separation between your subject and the background – although it’s a relatively small difference. But there are four ways to achieve shallow depth of field (DOF) with much older iPhones …

Portrait mode

The most obvious method is, of course, to use Portrait mode, which is specifically designed to allow people to be very clearly separated from the background.

This is a completely artificial effect using computational photography (assisted by LiDAR, on models that support it) to identify the subject and to apply an artificial blur to everything else. Early versions were extremely crude, but it’s become remarkably good in the last few years.

Macro shots

The second approach is Macro mode, which will be automatically enabled when you get extremely close to something. With this engaged, the iPhone selects the wide-angle camera, which can focus at extremely close distances.

In this mode, only a few centimetres will be in focus, with everything beyond it increasingly blurred. As you might notice from the example below, you should be prepared to spend a lot of time dusting and cleaning before attempting to photograph anything using this mode! You’ll know the mode is active when you see the yellow flower symbol in the bottom right of the display.

Getting close to the subject

You can also achieve a similar result with the standard camera by getting very close to the subject. For example:

Just tap on the object or person you want to be in focus before taking the photo.

Telephoto shots

A final factor affecting DOF is focal length. All else being equal, the longer the focal length, the shallower the depth of field, and so using the telephoto lens on an iPhone can allow us to achieve a somewhat blurred background.

Combining three methods

Combining three methods works best:

  • Select the telephoto lens
  • Get your subject as far away from the background as possible
  • Get as close as possible to your subject

This is the best approach to take when photographing people, and is especially effective with the iPhone 15 Pro and later due to the longer focal lengths.

Wrap-up

The wider and variable aperture lens is only one of the new camera features of the iPhone 18 Pro, so you may still want to upgrade if photography is a key application of your phone. But if background blur is your goal, there are other ways to achieve the same thing.
